prerequisites: Prior knowledge of general Mechanical Engineering aspects is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Upon successfully completing the course, the student will be able to know, understand, and apply the current regulations within the framework of road vehicles (passenger and industrial).
Upon successfully completing the course, the student will be able to write, sign, and develop R&D&i projects on road vehicles.

Upon successfully completing the course, the student will be able to know the operational characteristics and design and analyze the various elements and systems found in vehicles, both passenger and industrial types.
Upon successfully completing the course, the student will be able to conduct studies on active and passive safety in automobiles, through calculations, expert appraisals, or technical reports.

syllabus_topics: Regulatory framework. Vehicle homologation and modifications

assessment_methods.method: Reports on laboratory/computer practices and exercises (P)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for the theoretical block. The final theoretical grade is calculated as 0.7 * T, and the practical grade as 0.3 * P. If the theoretical minimum is met, the final grade is Theory + Practices; otherwise, it is the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. The extraordinary call follows the same evaluation system. For the differentiated evaluation model, a single written exam is given, consisting of a theoretical-practical part (T) and a practical part (P), with a minimum of 5 out of 10 required for the theoretical part; the final grade is calculated as (0.8 * T) + (0.2 * P).
